scene.metaphor: A disciplined machine casing that accepts swappable model modules through one standardized bay, showing how the API separates train, evaluate, and predict into different insertable parts.
scene.setting: A polished miniature studio lab built on a cool-gray workbench, with a low modular casing stretching laterally across the frame and lots of empty gray space around it.
scene.frozen_incident: Tal is calmly sliding a labeled module into the bay while a second module has just popped halfway out with a tiny mint-colored latch caught, implying harmless friction in the interface.
physical_materials: machined-looking charcoal resin casing with cobalt trim
one mint spring latch and one restrained warm coral module
scene.image_instruction: Create a polished editorial studio photograph of Tal Perry as the operator in a miniature machine-lab scene, recognizable with his curly dark hair, beard, and warm coral tank top translated into a tiny practical figurine. He stands left of a low charcoal casing, focused and faintly amused, one hand guiding a mint-accented module into a rigid bay while a second module has just nudged back out, caught on a small latch in a harmless, deadpan moment of friction. The metaphor should feel physical and exact: a reusable machine shell with three interchangeable blocks for train, evaluate, and predict, each rendered as a distinct chunky insert with subtle shape differences, no text. Keep the set tactile—foamcore base, resin body, brushed metal rails, felt inserts—and light it like premium product photography with cool-gray key light, cobalt highlights, and one restrained warm coral accent on Tal and a module. Compose laterally for a 3:1 banner, with one dominant subject, thick simple silhouettes, high tonal separation, and generous negative space so the idea still reads at thumbnail size.
